source: Appendix 3B codebook tables in the authoritative thesis DOCX

obedience_threshold.definition: A conceptualisation in which discipline is described as a requirement to obey, follow instructions or adjust to military expectations.
obedience_threshold.include: only when a speaker explicitly defines discipline through required obedience, instruction-following or adjustment to a stated military demand.
obedience_threshold.exclude: references to hierarchy, rules or punishment that do not define discipline through required obedience.
obedience_threshold.name: Required obedience

punishment_enforcement.definition: A conceptualisation in which punishment, sanction or enforcement is presented as a means through which obedience is expected to be secured or learnt.
punishment_enforcement.include: only when a speaker explicitly connects punishment, sanction or enforcement with obtaining or teaching obedient conduct.
punishment_enforcement.exclude: consequences that are merely mentioned, and claims about obedience that do not make punitive enforcement central.
punishment_enforcement.name: Punitive enforcement

hierarchy_authority.definition: A conceptualisation in which discipline is located in rank, higher authority, hierarchy or the military chain of command.
hierarchy_authority.include: when a speaker makes formal position or the chain of command part of what discipline means.
hierarchy_authority.exclude: trust, credibility or perceived legitimacy unless formal or positional authority is also central to the account.
hierarchy_authority.name: Formal authority

rule_order_tacit_norms.definition: A conceptualisation in which discipline is located in formal rules, legal order, stated instructions or unstated expectations.
rule_order_tacit_norms.include: when a speaker identifies a rule, instruction or tacit norm as part of the order through which discipline is understood.
rule_order_tacit_norms.exclude: a breach or sanction alone unless the account also identifies the rule or expectation against which conduct is judged.
rule_order_tacit_norms.name: Rules and tacit norms

breach_correction.definition: A conceptualisation in which an expectation becomes recognisable through an identified breach, error, detection or corrective response.
breach_correction.include: when a speaker uses breach, detection or correction to disclose what conduct was expected.
breach_correction.exclude: punishment presented as a general mechanism when the account does not identify an expectation revealed through breach or correction.
breach_correction.name: Correction after breach

authority_legitimacy_intent.definition: A conceptualisation in which willingness to obey is linked to how a subordinate reads the legitimacy, intent, reciprocity or non-arbitrariness of authority.
authority_legitimacy_intent.include: when a speaker explicitly connects obedience with recognising authority as legitimate, improving, reciprocal, credible or non-arbitrary.
authority_legitimacy_intent.exclude: rank alone and general expressions of trust that are not connected to a judgement about obeying authority.
authority_legitimacy_intent.name: Recognised authority and intent

authority_maintenance.definition: A conceptualisation in which authority is described as enacted, sustained, weakened or restored through ongoing conduct rather than conferred by rank alone.
authority_maintenance.include: when a speaker identifies interaction or conduct through which authority is maintained, undermined or re-established.
authority_maintenance.exclude: accounts that treat formal hierarchy or rank as sufficient and fixed.
authority_maintenance.name: Authority as enacted

trust_credibility.definition: A conceptualisation that connects discipline with trust, credibility, professionalism or confidence within the institution or before a public.
trust_credibility.include: when a speaker explicitly links discipline with being trusted, credible, professional or worthy of confidence.
trust_credibility.exclude: operational reliability unless trust or credibility is itself part of the speaker's claim.
trust_credibility.name: Trust and credibility

operational_reliability_risk.definition: A conceptualisation in which discipline is presented as relevant to reliable task performance or to avoiding an identified operational lapse.
operational_reliability_risk.include: when a speaker links discipline or its absence to completing a task, maintaining readiness or avoiding a specified organisational failure.
operational_reliability_risk.exclude: general claims about reputation, trust or good conduct that do not identify an operational concern.
operational_reliability_risk.name: Concern for operational reliability

non_negotiable_army_order.definition: A conceptualisation in which Army order is presented as given, functionally necessary or unavailable for negotiation within the account.
non_negotiable_army_order.include: when a speaker closes discussion of alternatives by presenting the military arrangement as necessary, designed for function or required to prevent failure.
non_negotiable_army_order.exclude: ordinary instruction-following unless the account expressly treats the wider order as necessary or beyond negotiation.
non_negotiable_army_order.name: Army order treated as necessary

innate_natural_claim.definition: A conceptualisation in which discipline is described as innate, natural, built in, uncodified or connected to survival rather than acquired through a stated process.
innate_natural_claim.include: only when the speaker explicitly locates the origin of discipline in nature, instinct, an inborn quality or a survival disposition.
innate_natural_claim.exclude: acquired habit, upbringing, training or socialisation.
innate_natural_claim.name: Discipline described as innate

prior_socialisation_mismatch.definition: A conceptualisation that relates discipline to a mismatch between prior upbringing, culture, community or exposure and military expectations.
prior_socialisation_mismatch.include: when a speaker identifies a prior form of socialisation and expressly contrasts it with the conduct expected in the programme or military setting.
prior_socialisation_mismatch.exclude: home values presented only as a positive source and accounts that do not identify a mismatch.
prior_socialisation_mismatch.name: Mismatch with prior socialisation

repetition_habit_memory.definition: A conceptualisation in which repeated practice is said to support habit, remembered action or reduced need for immediate prompting.
repetition_habit_memory.include: only when a speaker explicitly connects repetition, drill or consistency with habit, memory or ingrained conduct.
repetition_habit_memory.exclude: recurrence that is described only as externally required or supervised and is not linked to habit or memory.
repetition_habit_memory.name: Repetition described as habit-forming

goal_persistence.definition: A conceptualisation in which discipline means continuing towards an identified goal despite low desire, discomfort or another counter-inclination.
goal_persistence.include: when the account names both a goal and the counter-inclination through which the person is said to continue.
goal_persistence.exclude: routine repetition or endurance where no goal is identified.
goal_persistence.name: Goal-directed persistence

self_regulation_autonomy.definition: A conceptualisation in which discipline is described as self-control or action undertaken without immediate instruction, supervision or prompting.
self_regulation_autonomy.include: only when the speaker attributes regulation or action to the person rather than solely to an immediate external demand.
self_regulation_autonomy.exclude: visible compliance when the source does not claim self-regulation or reduced dependence on prompting.
self_regulation_autonomy.name: Self-regulation without immediate prompting

conformity_without_assent.definition: A conceptualisation in which outward conformity is treated as compatible with dissent, strategy, hostile intention or absence of inward agreement.
conformity_without_assent.include: when a speaker explicitly distinguishes what a person displays from what the person accepts, intends or believes.
conformity_without_assent.exclude: compliance alone when the source does not identify an appearance-assent distinction.
conformity_without_assent.name: Outward conformity without assent

extrinsic_motive_compliance.definition: A conceptualisation in which compliant conduct is attributed to fear, reward, ambition, graduation, status or another external incentive rather than inward formation.
extrinsic_motive_compliance.include: only when the speaker identifies an external motive and uses it to qualify the meaning of the observed compliance.
extrinsic_motive_compliance.exclude: self-stated goals or values unless the account expressly contrasts them with inward discipline.
extrinsic_motive_compliance.name: Extrinsically motivated compliance

self_discipline_personal_rule.definition: A conceptualisation in which self-discipline is described through personal rules, principles or self-control that guide conduct without an immediate external governor.
self_discipline_personal_rule.include: when the speaker describes the person as setting or applying a personal rule, principle or standard to their own conduct.
self_discipline_personal_rule.exclude: general autonomy when no personal form of governance is identified.
self_discipline_personal_rule.name: Self-discipline as personal governance

moral_neutral_discipline.definition: A conceptualisation that distinguishes technical control, precision or effectiveness from moral goodness.
moral_neutral_discipline.include: when a speaker explicitly presents disciplined conduct as potentially effective or controlled without therefore being morally good.
moral_neutral_discipline.exclude: ordinary wrongdoing, compliance or moral criticism that does not make this distinction.
moral_neutral_discipline.name: Moral neutrality of discipline

widened_life_governance.definition: A conceptualisation that extends discipline beyond military conduct to money, resources, thrift, restraint or another area of everyday life.
widened_life_governance.include: when the speaker applies the meaning of discipline to at least one stated non-military domain.
widened_life_governance.exclude: military-only conduct and narrow habits that are not used to extend the concept.
widened_life_governance.name: Discipline across everyday life

personal_responsibility_moralisation.definition: A conceptualisation in which discipline is used to judge, repair or govern the individual as personally responsible for conduct.
personal_responsibility_moralisation.include: when the speaker links discipline with personal blame, moral responsibility, correction of the person or a duty of self-government.
personal_responsibility_moralisation.exclude: practical self-management alone when the account does not moralise personal responsibility.
personal_responsibility_moralisation.name: Discipline as personal responsibility

prior_home_values.definition: A conceptualisation that traces discipline to family, home, cadets, early socialisation or another identified source preceding the programme.
prior_home_values.include: when a speaker identifies a specific prior source from which values, beliefs or disciplined conduct are said to have been learnt.
prior_home_values.exclude: general cultural mismatch and unspecified references to background.
prior_home_values.name: Discipline traced to prior values

context_observation_variability.definition: A conceptualisation in which discipline is described as varying across settings, roles, domains or conditions of observation.
context_observation_variability.include: when the speaker compares at least two contexts and identifies a difference in how discipline appears, is expected or is judged.
context_observation_variability.exclude: strategic display unless variation between contexts is itself the centre of the claim.
context_observation_variability.name: Contextual variation in discipline

strategic_display_persona.definition: A conceptualisation in which disciplined appearance is described as a role, persona or controlled presentation used to navigate a situation.
strategic_display_persona.include: when a speaker explicitly characterises the display as strategic, role-based, situational or intended to get by.
strategic_display_persona.exclude: ordinary visible signs when the source does not attribute a strategic presentation.
strategic_display_persona.name: Strategic performance of discipline

surveillance_visibility.definition: A conceptualisation that links disciplined conduct with being watched, inspected, guarded or kept visible.
surveillance_visibility.include: when observation or the possibility of observation is expressly connected to how conduct is displayed or adjusted.
surveillance_visibility.exclude: visible dress, posture or mannerisms when observation is not part of the account.
surveillance_visibility.name: Discipline under observation

visible_signs_legibility.definition: A conceptualisation in which discipline is judged through inspectable signs such as dress, deportment, neatness, mannerisms or etiquette.
visible_signs_legibility.include: when a speaker identifies a visible or audible sign as evidence by which discipline is recognised.
visible_signs_legibility.exclude: mechanisms of surveillance and public reputation unless the sign itself is the object of judgement.
visible_signs_legibility.name: Visible signs of discipline

standard_uncertainty_modelling.definition: A conceptualisation in which the standard for displaying or judging discipline is described as unclear, unevenly known, inconsistently modelled or dependent on role.
standard_uncertainty_modelling.include: when a speaker identifies uncertainty or inconsistency in the standard, its modelling or its application.
standard_uncertainty_modelling.exclude: rule ambiguity that does not concern how disciplined conduct is modelled or judged.
standard_uncertainty_modelling.name: Uncertain or inconsistently modelled standards

consequence_managed_compliance.definition: A conceptualisation in which visible compliance is described as maintained through stated consequences, reinforcement, rigid standards or pragmatic adjustment to external demand.
consequence_managed_compliance.include: when the account connects an external consequence or demand with the continuation of visible compliance.
consequence_managed_compliance.exclude: punishment as a general definition when the speaker does not centre managed visible compliance.
consequence_managed_compliance.name: Compliance managed through consequences

eye_service_appearance_gap.definition: A conceptualisation that distinguishes a disciplined appearance from what the speaker regards as substantive or real discipline.
eye_service_appearance_gap.include: when the source expressly contrasts how discipline looks with whether discipline is present beyond that appearance.
eye_service_appearance_gap.exclude: strategic performance when the source does not make an appearance-substance distinction.
eye_service_appearance_gap.name: Gap between appearance and substance

motivation_vs_discipline.definition: A conceptualisation that distinguishes effort under an audience, event, examination or immediate pressure from discipline understood as more durable conduct.
motivation_vs_discipline.include: when a speaker explicitly contrasts a temporary source of effort with a claim about discipline's duration.
motivation_vs_discipline.exclude: external motives generally unless the account makes the temporary-durable contrast.
motivation_vs_discipline.name: Temporary motivation versus durable discipline

unwatched_durability_test.definition: A conceptualisation in which the presence of discipline is judged by whether conduct continues when direct observation or inspection is absent.
unwatched_durability_test.include: when the account expressly uses an unwatched condition as a test of discipline.
unwatched_durability_test.exclude: general post-training persistence when absence of observation is not the stated test.
unwatched_durability_test.name: Discipline when unwatched

values_character_carrier.definition: A conceptualisation in which discipline is presented as carrying, grounding or enabling specified values or character traits.
values_character_carrier.include: when the speaker names a value or character trait and presents discipline as its carrier, ground or enabling condition.
values_character_carrier.exclude: general praise of values and claims about moral neutrality where no carrier relation is stated.
values_character_carrier.name: Discipline as a carrier of values

durability_after_control.definition: A conceptualisation concerned with whether disciplined conduct remains after training pressure, observation or institutional structure has weakened.
durability_after_control.include: when the speaker raises continuity across a stated reduction in control, supervision or structure.
durability_after_control.exclude: isolated unwatched moments and general hopes that discipline will last when no changed condition is identified.
durability_after_control.name: Discipline after control weakens

public_reputation_expectation.definition: A conceptualisation that connects disciplined appearance with public expectation, institutional reputation or expressed disappointment in the military.
public_reputation_expectation.include: when the speaker locates the judgement of discipline in a public audience or in the reputation of the institution.
public_reputation_expectation.exclude: internal trust and operational reliability unless public recognition or reputation is also central.
public_reputation_expectation.name: Discipline and public reputation

standard_setting.definition: A practice in which an authorised actor states, clarifies or imposes conduct expected within the programme.
standard_setting.include: a stated entry standard, rule, instruction, boundary or clarification of required conduct.
standard_setting.exclude: a response to failure unless the source also identifies the expectation against which conduct is judged.
standard_setting.name: Setting expected conduct

accountability_orientation.definition: A practice in which a recruit is required to account to authority, peers or the group for conduct or assigned responsibility.
accountability_orientation.include: reporting, accounting for self, answerability for a task or an explicit requirement to explain conduct.
accountability_orientation.exclude: visibility or observation alone when no requirement of answerability is identified.
accountability_orientation.name: Requiring answerability

consequence_linkage.definition: A practice in which specified conduct is linked to a stated punishment, reward, privilege, restriction, removal or staged consequence.
consequence_linkage.include: only when both the relevant conduct and the consequence attached to it are identified.
consequence_linkage.exclude: a general standard, threat or incentive when its relation to conduct is not stated.
consequence_linkage.name: Linking conduct to consequences

adaptation_timetable.definition: A practice in which expected conduct or tolerated difficulty is described as changing across a stated stage of training.
adaptation_timetable.include: comparisons between identified periods, such as an early and later week, where the expected response or tolerance differs.
adaptation_timetable.exclude: general claims of development that do not identify a time-staged change in expectation.
adaptation_timetable.name: Staging expectations over time

psychological_uncertainty.analytic_home: Using control to influence hearts and minds
psychological_uncertainty.definition: A practice in which information, observation conditions or the realism of an event is withheld, varied or staged, and presented as relevant to how recruits respond.
psychological_uncertainty.include: staged realism, false or withheld information, hidden observation, mystery or an explicitly described 'mind game'.
psychological_uncertainty.exclude: researcher uncertainty, ordinary confusion and ambiguity not organised by programme actors.
psychological_uncertainty.name: Managing uncertainty

symbolic_coercion.analytic_home: Using control to influence hearts and minds
symbolic_coercion.definition: A practice in which charged imagery, objects or language presents authority, danger, worth or punishment in intensified symbolic terms.
symbolic_coercion.include: a whip, ghost, slave-master image, death framing, declared unworthiness or another symbol whose severity is explicit in the source.
symbolic_coercion.exclude: an ordinary command, correction or object when the source does not give it symbolic force.
symbolic_coercion.name: Symbolic displays of severity

explanatory_reasoning.analytic_home: Using control to influence hearts and minds
explanatory_reasoning.definition: A practice in which an authorised actor supplies a reason, meaning or explanation for a disciplinary term, demand, correction or ordeal.
explanatory_reasoning.include: an explanation of titles, correction, pain, professional expectation or the stated purpose of a practice.
explanatory_reasoning.exclude: a bare command, label or assertion that supplies no reason or explanatory relation.
explanatory_reasoning.name: Explaining disciplinary practice

relational_influence.analytic_home: Using control to influence hearts and minds
relational_influence.definition: A practice in which trust, care, rapport, attachment or an approachable relationship is used in an attempt to guide conduct.
relational_influence.include: reasoning with youths, father-figure language, a described safe haven or another relationship explicitly connected to guidance.
relational_influence.exclude: encouragement, praise or motivation when no relationship is identified as part of the practice.
relational_influence.name: Relational guidance

motivational_activation.analytic_home: Using control to influence hearts and minds
motivational_activation.definition: A practice in which encouragement, challenge, morale or an affective appeal is used in an attempt to elicit effort or willingness.
motivational_activation.include: encouragement, energising war cries, morale-building challenge or language directed at willingness to continue.
motivational_activation.exclude: a reward attached as a consequence and collective ritual where repeated unity is the main feature.
motivational_activation.name: Affective encouragement

habit_repetition.analytic_home: Using control to influence hearts and minds
habit_repetition.definition: A practice in which the same word, drill, movement or command is repeated, with habit or automaticity stated as an intended or reported relation only where the source supports it.
habit_repetition.include: repeated drills, repeated 'sir' or repeated bodily commands; record habit only when the source explicitly links repetition with habit or reduced prompting.
habit_repetition.exclude: a single correction and do not infer habit from recurrence alone.
habit_repetition.name: Repetitive practice

persistence_beyond_training.definition: An expectation or question about whether conduct described as disciplined will continue beyond the immediate training setting.
persistence_beyond_training.include: statements about conduct after training, graduation or direct observation, provided the source presents persistence as expected, hoped for or uncertain.
persistence_beyond_training.exclude: evidence that deliberately examines conduct under a changed authority or setting; code that as testing persistence across conditions.
persistence_beyond_training.name: Anticipated persistence beyond training

habit_interruption.analytic_home: Using control to govern the individual body
habit_interruption.definition: A practice directed at interrupting a named civilian or prior bodily habit.
habit_interruption.include: a specified prior bodily habit and a programme action intended or described as interrupting it.
habit_interruption.exclude: repetition directed at establishing a new practice when no prior habit is identified.
habit_interruption.name: Disrupting prior bodily habits

bodily_regulation.analytic_home: Using control to govern the individual body
bodily_regulation.definition: A practice in which access to food, sleep, hydration, rest or bodily exertion is directed, limited or required by programme actors.
bodily_regulation.include: stated control of food, sleep, hydration, fatigue, pain, running, push-ups or injury under demand.
bodily_regulation.exclude: bodily appearance used as evidence and movement prescribed chiefly for standardised form.
bodily_regulation.name: Regulating bodily need and exertion

temporal_control.analytic_home: Using control to govern the individual body
temporal_control.definition: A practice in which access to time information, pacing or a temporal threshold is directed by programme actors.
temporal_control.include: withholding watches, paced hydration, timed action or removal at a stated temporal threshold.
temporal_control.exclude: the general sequence of training and time-staged expectations that do not control immediate pace or time information.
temporal_control.name: Controlling time and pace

embodied_standardisation.analytic_home: Using control to govern the individual body
embodied_standardisation.definition: A practice in which bodies are directed into a specified posture, movement, formation or configuration.
embodied_standardisation.include: a prescribed drill form, posture, position, crawl, placement of hands or other stated bodily configuration.
embodied_standardisation.exclude: observation of bodily signs when no attempt to prescribe or correct the bodily form is identified.
embodied_standardisation.name: Prescribing bodily form

bodily_sign_reading.analytic_home: Using control to govern the individual body
bodily_sign_reading.definition: A practice in which visible or audible bodily conduct is treated by an actor as evidence of discipline or its absence.
bodily_sign_reading.include: dress, voice, posture, neatness, use of 'sir' or another bodily sign explicitly read as evidence.
bodily_sign_reading.exclude: watching bodies for supervisory purposes when no sign is interpreted as evidence.
bodily_sign_reading.name: Reading bodily signs

visibility_supervision.definition: A practice in which conduct is placed within actual or anticipated observation, inspection or a stated line of sight.
visibility_supervision.include: scanning, inspection, hidden or announced observation and requirements that action remain visible or inspectable.
visibility_supervision.exclude: a bodily sign treated as evidence when the arrangement of visibility is not central.
visibility_supervision.name: Making conduct visible

bodily_proof.analytic_home: Using control to govern the individual body
bodily_proof.definition: A practice in which bodily evidence, footage or a staged visual representation is presented as proof of misconduct, danger or consequence.
bodily_proof.include: identified footage, a staged casualty or another bodily display used to establish a claim before recruits.
bodily_proof.exclude: ordinary supervision, inspection and bodily signs that are not presented as proof.
bodily_proof.name: Using bodily evidence

bodily_restriction.analytic_home: Using control to govern the individual body
bodily_restriction.definition: A practice in which movement, posture, equipment or bodily freedom is limited by programme actors.
bodily_restriction.include: confinement, removal of bootlaces or a belt, prolonged attention or another specified restriction.
bodily_restriction.exclude: physical exertion, prescribed drill form and ordinary movement commands when no restriction is identified.
bodily_restriction.name: Restricting bodily movement or equipment

coercive_correction.analytic_home: Using control to govern the individual body
coercive_correction.definition: A reported or observed practice involving forceful bodily correction that a source describes, questions or contests as coercive, abusive or torturous.
coercive_correction.include: draping, choking or another specified use of force where the source identifies coercion, abuse, torture or a comparable concern.
coercive_correction.exclude: ordinary commanded movement or exercise unless the source expressly marks force, coercion or contested bodily correction.
coercive_correction.name: Reported or contested physical coercion

durability_testing.definition: A practice or comparison that examines whether conduct continues after authority, setting, supervision or pressure has changed.
durability_testing.include: hidden rank, transfer to another unit, reduced supervision or another identified change used to examine persistence.
durability_testing.exclude: a general hope or expectation that conduct will last when no changed condition or comparison is identified.
durability_testing.name: Testing persistence across conditions

collective_accountability.analytic_home: Using control to tune the group
collective_accountability.definition: A practice in which a group is required to answer for, share the consequence of or respond to one member's conduct.
collective_accountability.include: a whole-platoon response to one recruit, a weakest-link demand or an explicit group consequence attached to individual conduct.
collective_accountability.exclude: peer monitoring or assistance when the group is not made answerable.
collective_accountability.name: Group answerability for individual conduct

lateral_surveillance.analytic_home: Using control to tune the group
lateral_surveillance.definition: A practice in which recruits are expected to observe one another's conduct, readiness or equipment.
lateral_surveillance.include: checking kit, noticing missing items or an explicit expectation to watch another recruit.
lateral_surveillance.exclude: formal instructor supervision and peer intervention when observation is not itself central.
lateral_surveillance.name: Peer monitoring

peer_correction.analytic_home: Using control to tune the group
peer_correction.definition: A practice in which recruits are expected to intervene in, correct or redirect another recruit's conduct.
peer_correction.include: a stated peer intervention, correction or effort to keep a recruit within a group expectation.
peer_correction.exclude: observation without intervention and formal correction delivered by programme authority.
peer_correction.name: Peer correction

reciprocal_obligation.analytic_home: Using control to tune the group
reciprocal_obligation.definition: A practice in which fairness, sharing, restraint, delegated responsibility or mutual duty organises conduct among group members.
reciprocal_obligation.include: sharing, fair allocation, leaders eating last, delegated peer responsibility or another explicit reciprocal duty.
reciprocal_obligation.exclude: collective punishment and general group belonging when no reciprocal responsibility is identified.
reciprocal_obligation.name: Reciprocal responsibility

equal_standard_enforcement.analytic_home: Using control to tune the group
equal_standard_enforcement.definition: A practice in which programme actors state or apply the same expected standard across identified categories of recruit.
equal_standard_enforcement.include: an explicit comparison across gender, role or another category together with a claim of no special treatment or equal correction.
equal_standard_enforcement.exclude: general standard-setting when no category comparison is present.
equal_standard_enforcement.name: Applying one standard across categories

competitive_pressure.analytic_home: Using control to tune the group
competitive_pressure.definition: A practice in which competition or rivalry is used to compare, rank or encourage performance between recruits or groups.
competitive_pressure.include: a stated contest, platoon rivalry, range competition or attempt to win that organises comparison.
competitive_pressure.exclude: collective encouragement or unity when no competitive comparison is identified.
competitive_pressure.name: Organising comparison through competition

factionalisation_risk.analytic_home: Using control to tune the group
factionalisation_risk.definition: A reported concern that rivalry, cheating or subgroup division may split the group or weaken shared order.
factionalisation_risk.include: an explicit concern about factions, subgroup division, gender split, cheating or rivalry that threatens group order.
factionalisation_risk.exclude: general instability and ordinary competition when the source does not identify a risk of subgroup fracture.
factionalisation_risk.name: Risk of group factionalisation

unstable_group_cohesion.analytic_home: Using control to tune the group
unstable_group_cohesion.definition: An account in which apparent group unity is described alongside fear, rivalry, controlled display, public insult or unequal treatment that qualifies that unity.
unstable_group_cohesion.include: only when the source provides evidence of both apparent cohesion and the condition that makes it fragile, coerced or unstable.
unstable_group_cohesion.exclude: clear expressions of cohesion and general group conflict when the tension between unity and instability is not established.
unstable_group_cohesion.name: Fragile or coerced cohesion

group_standard_imposition.analytic_home: Using control to tune the group
group_standard_imposition.definition: A practice in which an authorised actor sets a shared standard for the group and presents it as binding from above.
group_standard_imposition.include: an explicitly imposed platoon or group standard, particularly where its early or harsh establishment is identified.
group_standard_imposition.exclude: clarification of expected conduct generally when the source does not specify a shared group standard.
group_standard_imposition.name: Imposing a group standard

emulative_alignment.analytic_home: Using control to tune the group
emulative_alignment.definition: A practice or reported response in which recruits align visible conduct with an instructor's demonstrated appearance or action.
emulative_alignment.include: explicit copying or modelling of how an instructor looks, moves or acts.
emulative_alignment.exclude: obedience to a command and access to a model when no alignment or imitation is reported.
emulative_alignment.name: Alignment with instructor models

ritualised_unity.analytic_home: Using control to tune the group
ritualised_unity.definition: A practice in which a group repeatedly chants, counts, shouts or performs in unison, with unity stated as an intended or reported relation only where supported.
ritualised_unity.include: repeated war cries, chanting, counting in unison or another collective performance carried out together.
ritualised_unity.exclude: a shared symbol or one-off collective act, and do not infer unity from synchrony alone.
ritualised_unity.name: Repeated collective performance

symbolic_cohesion.analytic_home: Using control to tune the group
symbolic_cohesion.definition: A practice in which a shared name, symbol or identity frame is used to mark or invite group belonging.
symbolic_cohesion.include: platoon names, collective labels, citizenship language or another explicit symbol of shared identity.
symbolic_cohesion.exclude: repeated chants alone and do not infer cohesion unless belonging is stated or evidenced in the source.
symbolic_cohesion.name: Shared symbols of belonging

discipline_boundary_judgement.definition: A participant account that accepts, refuses, limits or redefines what an institutional practice may properly be called as discipline.
discipline_boundary_judgement.include: only when the participant makes an explicit judgement about the meaning, legitimacy or boundary of discipline, such as 'not discipline', 'torture' or 'a way to control'.
discipline_boundary_judgement.exclude: pain, dislike, compliance and criticism that do not also judge what should or should not count as discipline.
discipline_boundary_judgement.name: Judging the boundaries of discipline

bodily_harm_danger.definition: A participant account of a discrete bodily injury, illness, violation, near-fatal event or perceived risk of serious physical harm.
bodily_harm_danger.include: a reported infection, burn, bleeding, near drowning, taped-mask danger, injury, bodily violation or explicit fear that a practice could kill or seriously harm.
bodily_harm_danger.exclude: cumulative hunger, sleep loss, exertion or collapse without a discrete harmful event; code those as reported depletion or exhaustion.
bodily_harm_danger.name: Reported bodily harm or danger

depletion_exhaustion.definition: A participant account of cumulative bodily depletion through hunger, sleep loss, prolonged exertion, shutdown or collapse.
depletion_exhaustion.include: sustained deprivation, exhaustion, lack of sleep, hunger, bodily shutdown or people dropping or collapsing where accumulation is central.
depletion_exhaustion.exclude: a single injury, illness or dangerous incident unless cumulative depletion is also the main experiential claim.
depletion_exhaustion.name: Reported depletion or exhaustion

psychological_wounding.definition: A participant account of fear, grief, confusion, lowered self-regard, despair, emotional breaking or another form of psychological distress.
psychological_wounding.include: only where the participant directly describes psychic hurt, emotional collapse, traumatic persistence or a self experienced as frightened, confused, isolated or broken.
psychological_wounding.exclude: later identity change and inferred mental injury when the participant does not report distress or its persistence.
psychological_wounding.name: Reported psychological distress

verbal_degradation.definition: A participant account of speech experienced as degrading through insult, cursing, attack on family, animalising language or another demeaning form of address.
verbal_degradation.include: the reported words or a sufficiently specific description of degrading speech by peers or authority.
verbal_degradation.exclude: general rudeness and identity-specific degradation centred on race, colour, place, slavery or inherited identity; code the latter as reported racialised degradation.
verbal_degradation.name: Reported verbal degradation

racialised_degradation.definition: A participant account of language or treatment experienced as degrading through race, colour, place, slavery, mixed identity or another inherited identity marker.
racialised_degradation.include: a specific identity-marked expression or treatment, such as 'field slave', colourism, 'coolie' or place-based degradation, where that meaning is central.
racialised_degradation.exclude: general insult, hierarchy and abusive language when no racialised, colonial, slavery-linked or inherited identity meaning is identified.
racialised_degradation.name: Reported racialised degradation

humiliation_display.definition: A participant account of being singled out, exposed, made to fail or visibly subordinated before others in a way experienced as humiliating.
humiliation_display.include: both a public or witnessed setting and the participant's account of shame, diminishment or displayed subordination.
humiliation_display.exclude: private pain, ordinary correction and exclusion when public display or humiliation is not central.
humiliation_display.name: Reported public humiliation

silencing_nonresponse.analytic_home: Disconnecting from previous life; Reconnecting inside the programme
silencing_nonresponse.definition: A participant account in which an explanation, report, self-defence or request to be heard is blocked, ignored or treated as illegitimate.
silencing_nonresponse.include: a stated attempt to speak, explain, report or defend together with the response or condition that denied a hearing.
silencing_nonresponse.exclude: privacy loss, gossip and peer betrayal when the central issue is not the denial of voice or response.
silencing_nonresponse.name: Reported denial of voice

family_separation_priority.definition: A participant account in which programme demands separate the participant from family contact or place institutional work above a stated family relation.
family_separation_priority.include: denied calls, separation from a child, a stated priority of work over kin or another reported restriction of family contact.
family_separation_priority.exclude: family as a reason to persist, provide or imagine a future; code that as kin-oriented motivation.
family_separation_priority.name: Reported family separation or subordination

peer_care_solidarity.definition: A participant account of care, practical help, loyalty, companionship or shared endurance among peers.
peer_care_solidarity.include: a specific act or relation of peer care, such as washing for an injured peer, bringing food, holding on together or sustained companionship.
peer_care_solidarity.exclude: group victory, collective reputation and external validation when care or solidarity is not the centre of the account.
peer_care_solidarity.name: Reported peer care and solidarity

group_pride_validation.definition: A participant account in which collective achievement, recognition or shared performance is experienced as validating the group.
group_pride_validation.include: a named group achievement, successful inspection, competition or recognition together with expressed shared pride or validation.
group_pride_validation.exclude: individual pride in personal change and group activity without expressed collective validation.
group_pride_validation.name: Reported group pride and validation

respect_recognition.definition: A participant account of being respected, praised, protected or recognised, or of respect being withheld, conditional or denied.
respect_recognition.include: reciprocal respect, praise, protection, dignity recognition or a sufficiently specific account of withheld or conditional recognition.
respect_recognition.exclude: teaching or paced assistance where helping the participant learn is the central relation.
respect_recognition.name: Reported respect or misrecognition

learning_support.definition: A participant account of explanation, patience, knowledge, attention or care directed at helping the participant understand or perform a task.
learning_support.include: a specific act of teaching, explanation, checking understanding, paced assistance or additional time offered for learning.
learning_support.exclude: routine instruction, praise and a skill outcome when the supportive pedagogic relation is not identified.
learning_support.name: Reported learning support

needed_responsibility.definition: A participant account in which delegated responsibility is experienced as trust, usefulness, competence or being needed within the programme.
needed_responsibility.include: an identified responsibility, such as keys, stores, tanks, protection or peer leadership, together with the participant's stated sense of trust, usefulness or agency.
needed_responsibility.exclude: responsibility directed mainly towards family outside the programme and assigned tasks that carry no reported meaning of trust or usefulness.
needed_responsibility.name: Felt trust through responsibility

exclusion_isolation.definition: A participant account of rejection, ejection, physical pushing away, isolation or being left alone within the programme.
exclusion_isolation.include: a specific act or condition through which the participant describes being excluded, ejected, pushed away or isolated.
exclusion_isolation.exclude: self-chosen withdrawal undertaken for safety or dignity; code that as a self-protective boundary or refusal.
exclusion_isolation.name: Reported exclusion or isolation

peer_mistrust_betrayal.analytic_home: Disconnecting from previous life; Reconnecting inside the programme
peer_mistrust_betrayal.definition: A participant account in which theft, threat, gossip, privacy violation or broken loyalty makes a peer relation feel unsafe or untrustworthy.
peer_mistrust_betrayal.include: a stated peer act and the participant's account of mistrust, betrayal, threat or broken loyalty.
peer_mistrust_betrayal.exclude: collective blame or pressure arising chiefly from a group-order mechanism; code that as reported group fragmentation.
peer_mistrust_betrayal.name: Reported peer mistrust or betrayal

authority_disregard.analytic_home: Disconnecting from previous life; Reconnecting inside the programme
authority_disregard.definition: A participant account in which an authority response is experienced as ignoring, minimising or inadequately addressing bodily pain, medical distress, grief or another stated vulnerability.
authority_disregard.include: both a disclosed vulnerability and the authority response that the participant describes as disregard, minimisation or withheld care.
authority_disregard.exclude: blocked explanation when the central issue is denial of voice rather than the response to vulnerability.
authority_disregard.name: Reported disregard of vulnerability

structural_powerlessness.definition: A participant account that locates limited agency, low standing or ineffective formal responsibility within the programme's hierarchy or structure.
structural_powerlessness.include: an explicit positional account, such as being at the bottom, having 'little power' or holding responsibility without effective authority.
structural_powerlessness.exclude: a single disrespectful interaction and inferred powerlessness where the participant does not identify a wider positional or structural limit.
structural_powerlessness.name: Reported limited agency within hierarchy

group_fragmentation.definition: A participant account in which collective punishment, lateral blame or group pressure is described as turning peers against one another or weakening belonging.
group_fragmentation.include: a specific group-order mechanism and the reported division, blame, ejection pressure or weakened belonging associated with it.
group_fragmentation.exclude: theft, threat, gossip and interpersonal betrayal when no collective punishment or group-pressure mechanism is identified.
group_fragmentation.name: Reported group fragmentation

self_protection_boundary.analytic_home: Reconnecting inside the programme; Developing within a precarious situation
self_protection_boundary.definition: A participant account of reaching a stated safety or dignity limit and seeking to refuse, leave, withdraw or protect the self.
self_protection_boundary.include: an explicit boundary, refusal, wish to leave or protective action connected to safety, dignity or unacceptable treatment.
self_protection_boundary.exclude: disagreement generally and assertions of continuing identity where no protective boundary or action is identified.
self_protection_boundary.name: Self-protective boundary or refusal

temporal_disruption.definition: A participant account of programme time as counted yet indefinite, repetitive, prescribed, emotionally heavy or separated from ordinary rhythm.
temporal_disruption.include: calendars, uncertain end dates, endless days, prescribed cycles or repeated punishment when the participant's experience of time is central.
temporal_disruption.exclude: repeated schedules described chiefly as embodied routine or a personal timetable.
temporal_disruption.name: Experience of institutional time

routine_internalisation.definition: A participant account in which a repeated schedule or standard is described as habitual, embodied or carried with reduced external prompting.
routine_internalisation.include: waking early, making beds, punctual reporting or another repeated practice only when the participant describes habit, embodiment or continuation with reduced prompting.
routine_internalisation.exclude: recurrence alone, commanded performance and researcher inference of inward formation.
routine_internalisation.name: Reported embodied routine

endurance_conditioning.definition: A participant account of concealing emotion, acting through discomfort, entering a survival mode or persisting under pressure.
endurance_conditioning.include: hiding tears, pushing through, acting by instinct under threat, describing survival mode or another explicit account of endurance.
endurance_conditioning.exclude: general positive change and do not infer conditioning, capability or lasting resilience from endurance in one situation.
endurance_conditioning.name: Reported endurance under pressure

reframing_as_training.definition: A participant account that later reinterprets a punishment, hardship or painful practice as preparation, useful training, pressure or a form of building.
reframing_as_training.include: an explicit retrospective reinterpretation by the participant, such as 'not punishment but extra training' or 'building me'.
reframing_as_training.exclude: an institutional claim that hardship is useful unless the participant adopts or develops that interpretation.
reframing_as_training.name: Retrospective reframing as training

practical_competence.definition: A participant account of acquiring or being able to exercise a named practical skill or work capacity through programme activity.
practical_competence.include: a specific capacity, such as cooking, stores work, tank duties, tool use, driving or truck work, together with an acquisition or ability claim.
practical_competence.exclude: general maturity, confidence, routine compliance and identity claims without a specified practical capacity.
practical_competence.name: Reported practical competence

positive_transformation.definition: A participant account that presents change in largely affirmative terms, such as greater maturity, pride, peace, confidence, discipline or capability.
positive_transformation.include: a direct positive before-after or becoming claim made by the participant.
positive_transformation.exclude: change that remains inseparable from harm, contradiction or unresolved negative meaning; code that as reported ambivalent or unresolved change.
positive_transformation.name: Reported positive change

ambivalent_unresolved_change.definition: A participant account in which positive and negative meanings of change remain together without resolution.
ambivalent_unresolved_change.include: paired claims of growth and harm, hope and darkness, or good and bad change where neither side is resolved by the account.
ambivalent_unresolved_change.exclude: a settled positive account, a settled harmful account and complexity supplied only by the researcher.
ambivalent_unresolved_change.name: Reported ambivalent or unresolved change

dangerous_becoming.definition: A participant account expressing concern that programme formation may support superiority, dehumanisation, violence, robotic conduct, narrowed judgement or alienation from civilians or kin.
dangerous_becoming.include: an explicit warning, perception or example connecting the programme with one of these possible forms of harmful becoming.
dangerous_becoming.exclude: bodily danger during a particular event and do not infer a harmful outcome that the participant does not claim.
dangerous_becoming.name: Concern about harmful formation

identity_continuity_resistance.analytic_home: Disconnecting from previous life; Developing within a precarious situation
identity_continuity_resistance.definition: A participant account asserting that humanity, prior competence, inward judgement or another aspect of self remained despite institutional attempts or pressures to remake conduct.
identity_continuity_resistance.include: an explicit continuity claim, such as retaining a mind of one's own, prior competence, humanity or an inward source of discipline.
identity_continuity_resistance.exclude: a judgement about what should count as discipline when continuity of self is not also asserted.
identity_continuity_resistance.name: Reported continuity of self

kin_motivation.definition: A participant account in which attachment or obligation to family supplies a stated reason to persist, provide, succeed or imagine a future.
kin_motivation.include: making a family member proud, providing for a child, sacrificing for a sibling or another explicit kin-centred reason for action.
kin_motivation.exclude: family contact that is blocked or subordinated by programme demands; code that as reported family separation or subordination.
kin_motivation.name: Kin-oriented motivation

principle_purpose_orientation.definition: A participant account that locates action or discipline in an inwardly endorsed principle, purpose, belief, moral commitment or self-directed standard.
principle_purpose_orientation.include: an explicit reference to discipline 'from within', moral purpose, belief, roots, self-directed improvement or another personally endorsed standard.
principle_purpose_orientation.exclude: motives centred chiefly on kin, reward, fear or a future outside the programme.
principle_purpose_orientation.name: Self-reported principle or purpose

alternative_oppositional_future.definition: A participant account that makes visible a future outside, away from or critical of the programme's military or disciplinary terms.
alternative_oppositional_future.include: a named alternative vocation, care- or family-oriented path, refusal of an institutional identity or another explicit future beyond programme terms.
alternative_oppositional_future.exclude: uncertainty, dissatisfaction and criticism that do not disclose an alternative or oppositional future.
alternative_oppositional_future.name: Imagined future beyond programme terms

hope_resilience.analytic_home: Disconnecting from previous life; Reconnecting inside the programme; Developing within a precarious situation
hope_resilience.definition: A participant account or visual expression in which hope, light, fire, peace, rising or refusal to be fully reduced remains present alongside vulnerability or unresolved difficulty.
hope_resilience.include: an explicit phrase, image or experiential claim of hope or resilience, including a painting that retains possibility amid darkness.
hope_resilience.exclude: general positive change and researcher-attributed resilience when the participant or visual material does not express it.
hope_resilience.name: Expressed hope or resilience

AUTHORITY_HUB.name: Authority
AUTHORITY_HUB.definition: Synthetic integrative device connecting conceptualisation, operationalisation and experience across Chapters 5, 6 and 7.
AUTHORITY_HUB.include: The authority-related code nodes listed below.
AUTHORITY_HUB.exclude: Interpretation as a raw ENA code or independently coded evidence.
